key_insight: Introduce a training-free evidential memory layer that sits on top of frozen view-conditioned 3D generators to fuse information across a monocular video stream, producing temporally consistent multi-view 3D reconstructions.
problem_solved: Per-frame application of single-view 3D generators yields temporally inconsistent (flickering/incoherent) reconstructions when fed long monocular streams; Stream3D resolves this by aggregating evidence over time for stable outputs.
method: Evidential memory: maintain a compact, uncertainty-aware memory that accumulates per-frame evidence about geometry/appearance and tracks confidence over time.

Memory-conditioned generation: at each incoming frame, combine the current view with the evidential memory to condition a frozen view-conditioned 3D generator, producing temporally coherent reconstructions without retraining.

Lightweight, sequential updates: update memory with new evidence and uncertainty using principled fusion rules so the pipeline remains training-free and compatible with off-the-shelf generators (e.g., SAM 3D, TRELLIS, Hunyuan3D).
impact: Enables robust, temporally consistent 3D reconstruction from long monocular streams using existing generators—reducing flicker and improving deployment practicality for robotics, AR/VR, and streaming perception without costly retraining.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: monocular stream → evidential memory (update loop) → frozen generator → consistent 3D output
Before vs. after sequence: side-by-side temporal frames showing per-frame generator outputs (flickery) vs. Stream3D outputs (stable)
Memory visualization: heatmap/uncertainty map over time illustrating evidence accumulation and confidence evolution
Architecture icon set: small symbols for 'frozen generator', 'memory module', and 'sequential fusion' to show modularity & training-free nature
paper_title: Stream3D: Sequential Multi-View 3D Generation via Evidential Memory
paper_authors: Kaichen Zhou, Zeyang Bai, Xinhai Chang, Mengyu Wang, Paul Liang
